items.title: The lobotomy was awarded a Nobel Prize
items.claim: Egas Moniz won the 1949 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his discovery of the therapeutic value of the prefrontal leucotomy (lobotomy). What's the modern status?

options.text: The procedure remains a first-line treatment

Lobotomy is no longer performed; thousands of patients (around 40,000-50,000 in the US alone, 1936-50s) suffered permanent personality damage. Modern psychosurgery is far more targeted (deep brain stimulation, cingulotomy for refractory OCD)

items.reveal_title: An honoured procedure that caused immense harm
items.reveal:
Walter Freeman performed perhaps 3,500 of his transorbital 'icepick' lobotomies in the US through the 1950s. Patients included Rosemary Kennedy (1941, permanently incapacitated) and many institutionalised individuals.

The procedure declined rapidly after chlorpromazine (1952) provided pharmacological alternatives. Calls to revoke Moniz's Nobel continue. Modern functional neurosurgery (capsulotomy, cingulotomy, deep brain stimulation) targets specific circuits with imaging guidance and is reversible (in DBS).
items.why: Therapeutic enthusiasm without rigorous evidence can produce widespread harm. Modern evidence-based standards exist because of cases like this.

items.title: Bowlby's 44 thieves
items.claim: John Bowlby's 1944 '44 Juvenile Thieves' study linked maternal separation to later antisocial behaviour. What is a key methodological criticism made of it today?

options.text: The sample was very large and well controlled
Bowlby personally interviewed the children, risking confirmation bias, and the sample was small
It was a randomised controlled trial

items.reveal:
Bowlby studied 44 juvenile thieves and 44 controls at his clinic, conducting assessments himself. Critics note the risk of bias and the difficulty of separating maternal deprivation from broader disadvantage.

Rutter (1981) drew the influential distinction between privation and deprivation.
items.why: Foundational studies often used methods we would now strengthen, but they framed questions that still drive research.
